meta.name: GetHired Project Ideas — Bank
meta.note: Static, gap-tied project ideas (V4-P5). Each idea is tagged to the CV/assessment category it addresses so the Roadmap can surface only ideas relevant to a person's actual current gaps, and role-tagged the same way lib/mcq's questions are (every idea includes 'generalist'; specific tracks are added only where the project is genuinely central to that track's day-to-day). `externalLink` is only set when one of this project's own existing public labs.sarathg.me guides genuinely fits the idea — not every idea has one, and no idea links to an unlisted/non-navigable page on that site (only osint.html, shopeasy.html, wazuh.html, pivoting.html are wired into that site's navbar/sitemap; other pages found in that repo during this session were not linked anywhere on the live site, so were left alone rather than surfaced here).
meta.categories_with_no_project_ideas: certifications and soft_skills have no entries here on purpose — earning a cert or polishing a CV isn't a 'build something' project, so those roadmap stages simply show no project-ideas panel, which is the honest behavior rather than forcing a fit.

projects.title: Stand up a home SIEM and triage your own alerts
projects.description: Deploy a free SIEM, generate some real attack traffic against a test VM, and practice reading what actually shows up in the dashboard — the same log-analysis muscle interviewers ask about.

projects.title: Get hands-on with a SIEM's own query/search language
projects.description: Instead of only reading pre-built dashboards, write your own searches and detection rules against generated log data — tool fluency, not just tool familiarity.

projects.title: Set up a two-network lab and practice pivoting
projects.description: Build a small two-network VM lab and practice routing traffic between segments with port forwarding and tunneling — hands-on reinforcement of exactly what the networking checkpoints test.

projects.title: Turn a lateral-movement exercise into an incident report
projects.description: After working through a pivoting/lateral-movement lab, write it up backwards as if you were the defender who caught it after the fact — what indicators you'd have seen, in what order, and what you'd escalate.

projects.title: Find and document real vulnerabilities in a deliberately vulnerable app
projects.description: Work through a vulnerable-vs-fixed version of the same app, find as many bugs as you can on the vulnerable side, then read the fixed code to see exactly what changed — builds the pattern recognition the vulnerability-ID checkpoints test.

projects.title: Build your own OWASP Top 10 checklist from a real attack
projects.description: Attack a vulnerable app — broken auth, JWT flaws, IDOR/BOLA — and for each bug you find, write down which OWASP Top 10 category it maps to and why. Turns a memorized list into a checklist you actually understand.

projects.title: Run a full scan-to-report workflow against a vulnerable target
projects.description: Recon with a port scanner, manual testing with an intercepting proxy, then write the findings up like a real report — the actual tool workflow entry-level pentest roles expect on day one.

projects.title: Run a full OSINT recon pass and write it up
projects.description: Work through open-source recon techniques — search operators, reverse image search, WHOIS, social footprint — against a consenting target (yourself or a friend who's opted in), and compile the findings into a short recon report.

projects.title: Map a real attack chain to MITRE ATT&CK
projects.description: Pick a public breach writeup or your own home-lab exercise and map each stage to a MITRE ATT&CK tactic/technique. This is exactly the framework fluency SOC and generalist roles are expected to show on day one.

projects.title: Write a script that parses and summarizes a raw log file
projects.description: Take a raw auth log or web-server log and write a short script that automatically extracts failed-login patterns or suspicious IPs — the kind of small automation that saves real triage time.

projects.title: Script one repetitive recon step
projects.description: Pick one manual step from a pentest workflow — subdomain enumeration, port-scan result parsing, that kind of thing — and script it. Even a small, real script is a genuine differentiator on an entry-level CV.

projects.title: Configure a firewall/router lab from scratch
projects.description: Set up a small virtual network, write real ACL and firewall rules, and document why each rule exists — direct, hands-on practice with the tools category checkpoints assess for a network-security track.
